quarterly_data.signal: CSO: EVX-04 (off-the-shelf AML vaccine) has completed target discovery and selected its lead, and is now in IND-enabling activities including GMP manufacturing while engaging clinical sites; CEO: clinical sites, protocol development, GMP production and compiling the regulatory documentation are all ongoing and on track, with no change to the publicly stated timeframe; CSO: on track with the communicated timeline of a regulatory filing by the end of the year. CSO: the company plans to take EVX-04 into the clinic while engaging with companies, and this is not necessarily dependent on entering a partnership.

CSO: EVX-05 (glioblastoma) has concluded target discovery; several vaccine candidates have been designed and are being experimentally tested to select the lead, to be followed by IND-enabling activities and a first-in-human study with Duke University. No firm timelines have been communicated, as lead selection must come first, and the trial design has not been entirely settled (patients not benefiting from classical chemotherapy might be one option).

CSO: new preclinical data for the EVX-V1 cytomegalovirus (CMV) vaccine program, presented at the International Herpesvirus Workshop in July, show that T-cell epitopes discovered with AI-Immunology have the potential to control acute infection, latency and reactivation in CMV-infected mice; this complements earlier results showing that both novel and optimized known B-cell antigens reduce viral infection, and the data will guide antigen selection for a broadly protective CMV vaccine candidate.

CSO: AI-Immunology is clinically validated with a positive outcome in three out of three oncology trials, and supports multiple modalities including peptides, recombinant proteins, DNA and RNA. CEO: the company is in active partnership conversations on its programs and platform.
